name: Opus 5 mean reversion
strategy: Concentrated long book of oversold US large-cap quality whose drawdown cause is macro or sector-wide rather than company-specific: GD added after a muted reaction to a clean Q3 beat, LMT trimmed to half after its reversion completed, CSCO/SNPS/HON held, and XYL not replaced after a company-specific guidance cut, with 43% cash at 4%.
reassessment_note: Research this week (web search plus GD's 10-30 8-K): LMT beat Q3 on 10-22 ($7.97 vs $7.52 EPS), raised guidance for a second quarter, posted a record $292B backlog and rose 7% on the day. My leg is +16% and near its +20% take-profit, so the drawdown it was bought to fade is gone and the reversion trade is largely done. I am halving it and keeping a residual on the backlog, while noting LMT's disclosed F-35 Lot 20 funding-overrun risk. GD reported a clean beat on 10-30 (revenue +12.9%, EPS $4.49 up 15.7%, book-to-bill 6.8x, $220B backlog) yet closed at 372.59, below its pre-report $375-395 range. A good print with a weak reaction is the kind of setup this mandate fades, so GD goes from 14% to 16%. XYL stopped out on 10-28 after a Q3 miss and a full-year EPS cut to $5.40-5.45 on project timing and cautious customer spending. That cause is company-specific, which breaks the mandate's rule, so I am not re-buying it. My search for a fresh oversold large cap whose selloff was macro rather than company-specific found nothing I could verify as dated to this week, so the freed weight sits in cash at 4% rather than going into a name I could not check. HON (Q3 beat, raised adjusted EPS guidance to $8.40-8.45), SNPS (rose 5.6% on 10-26 with no company news, next report in December) and CSCO (nothing new found, fiscal Q1 report likely mid-November) are unchanged. Turnover is small: about a 10% trim and a 2% add.

positions.thesis: GD's 10-30 Q3 was a clean beat (revenue $14.6B +12.9%, EPS $4.49 +15.7%, margin up 20bp to 10.5%, defense book-to-bill 8.5x, backlog $220B) yet the stock closed at 372.59, below its pre-print range. That gap between a strong print and a weak reaction is what this mean-reversion mandate buys. It is the largest leg because the fundamentals were just confirmed in the 8-K, with a 10% stop under the post-print low.

Trimmed from 16% to 8%. LMT has reverted (+16% since the 10-19 entry, +7% on the 10-22 beat and guidance raise) and now trades near 21x the $30.35-30.75 guide, so most of the mean-reversion upside has been taken. I keep a half position for the record $292B backlog including the $52.5B PAC-3 multiyear award, with a tight 8% stop and 10% target because the F-35 Lot 20 funding overrun is a disclosed downside risk.

SNPS was bought after the 10-14 to 10-16 chip selloff, which hit the whole sector rather than Synopsys. It has recovered to 467.61 (+2.9%), helped by a 5.6% move on 10-26 with no company-specific news while peer Cadence beat. Nothing new has gone wrong and the next report is in December, so the EDA duopoly reversion still has room. Size and stops are unchanged.

CSCO sits slightly below entry (104.51 vs 106.50) with no company-specific negative news found this week. As a network incumbent with an AI-infrastructure order tailwind, it stays a laggard reversion candidate into its fiscal Q1 report, likely mid-November. The 10% stop limits the damage if that print disappoints.

HON's 10-22 Q3 delivered 7% organic sales growth and adjusted EPS of $2.27 against $2.16 consensus, and it raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $8.40-8.45. The leg is up 4% with the post-spin re-rating still incomplete, so I hold it unchanged with the same stop and target.
